bluf: JUNETEENTH — City holiday with major events citywide. Threat posture ELEVATED on four domains: Juneteenth Parade (E. 12th/MLK, 10 AM–noon) + Kali Uchis at Germania Amphitheater (~14,000, 7 PM, outdoor) + Music Under the Stars at Capitol Mall (7–9 PM). Road closures east of I-35 from ~8 AM. Flash flood risk (Level 2/4, storms possible tonight) and heat index up to 106°F. US-Iran Burgenstock talks POSTPONED — Iran hardliners pulled out, Israel resumed Lebanon airstrikes. Monitor for domestic protest reactions. Robbery-homicide suspect from E. Riverside still at large.

incidents.title: Robbery-Homicide — E. Riverside AutoZone (SUSPECT AT LARGE)
incidents.detail: APD released new video June 18 of suspect wanted in the fatal shooting of Jose Salgado-Amador, 28, during a robbery at the E. Riverside AutoZone parking lot. Suspect: Hispanic male, 15–20, gray hoodie, fled in a light-colored sedan. Case is Austin's 27th homicide of 2026. Suspect remains unidentified and at large. $1,000 reward active. Suspect at large with lethal-force robbery history. Brief ALL valet, bellstand, and exterior staff. Report suspicious loitering to APD Crime Stoppers (512) 472-8477.

incidents.title: SE Austin Homicide Victim Identified — Francesca Ortiz, 40
incidents.location: Waters at Bluff Springs, 7707 S I-35 Service Rd NB
incidents.detail: APD identified the woman found dead at Waters at Bluff Springs on June 17 as Francesca Ortiz, age 40. Case is Austin's 29th homicide of 2026. APD investigation ongoing; no suspect identified. Third in a SE Austin homicide cluster this week. No direct threat to property. Situational awareness for staff commuting on S. I-35 service road. No suspect or connection to downtown.

incidents.title: I-35 Hit-and-Run Arrest — Suspect Identified
incidents.detail: APD arrested a woman in connection with the hit-and-run crash that killed a pedestrian on the downtown I-35 service road on June 13. Suspect is in custody. Case closed for active threat purposes. Positive development — active threat from at-large vehicle suspect resolved. No direct impact to property.

incidents.title: West Campus Serial Burglar/Assault Arrested — Octavius Brown
incidents.detail: APD arrested Octavius Brown, a repeat offender, for three apartment break-ins on West Campus (June 10) including a sexual assault of a sleeping victim. Brown was recently released from jail in April and admitted to the crimes. Charged with burglary of habitation with intent to commit sex offense. Currently in Travis County Jail. Primarily a UT-area threat. Brown is in custody — no direct ongoing threat to property. Awareness flag: Juneteenth crowds near campus create opportunity for similar predatory activity. Brief front desk staff on suspicious behavior protocols.

incidents.title: US–Iran Burgenstock Talks POSTPONED — MOU Under Pressure
incidents.detail: The US-Iran implementation talks at Burgenstock have been POSTPONED. Iran's IRGC hardliners objected to a public ceremony with US officials; JD Vance cancelled his Switzerland trip. Iran has reportedly suspended the 60-day negotiation window. Separately, Israel resumed airstrikes on Lebanon (16+ killed Friday), accusing Hezbollah of ceasefire violations. The MOU remains electronically signed (June 18) but implementation is now in jeopardy. Strait of Hormuz remains open per MOU terms. ELEVATED watch for domestic protest activity today. Both pro-Iran groups (angered by Israeli attacks) and anti-Iran groups (concerned about deal collapse) may demonstrate. Juneteenth crowds provide cover for larger gatherings. Monitor Capitol area and UT. Notify Director of Security of any organized demonstrations approaching downtown.

civil_unrest.title: Juneteenth Parade & Events — East Austin (ROAD CLOSURES IN EFFECT)
civil_unrest.location: E. 12th Street / MLK Blvd, East Austin
civil_unrest.detail: Juneteenth Parade runs 10 AM–noon along E. 12th Street and MLK Blvd. Road closures east of I-35 in effect beginning ~8 AM. AACHF Fun Run at 1300 E. MLK & Leona St (morning). All-day festival at Rosewood Neighborhood Park, 2300 Rosewood Ave. Music Under the Stars at Capitol Mall Amphitheater (Bullock Museum) 7–9 PM — Rochelle & the Sidewinders (7 PM), Tameca Jones (8 PM). City of Austin, City courts, UT Austin, Travis County offices ALL CLOSED. Large crowds expected throughout day in East Austin; some dispersal to downtown after parade.

civil_unrest.title: US–Iran MOU Collapse Watch — Protest Potential ELEVATED
civil_unrest.location: Downtown Austin / Capitol / UT Austin Campus
civil_unrest.detail: Burgenstock talks postponed, Israel resumed Lebanon airstrikes (16+ killed Friday). This combination creates elevated risk of spontaneous protest activity — pro-Palestinian and anti-Iran factions both have motivation to demonstrate. No confirmed organized protest events in Austin, but Juneteenth crowds citywide provide assembly opportunity. Monitor social media for pop-up activity near Capitol, UT campus, or Congress Ave. APD likely has augmented Juneteenth presence downtown.

notes: Heat index values up to 106°F this afternoon. Heat Advisory remains in effect through Saturday evening for parts of the Austin area.

FLASH FLOOD RISK: Severe Weather Outlook Level 2/4 for central Texas. Cold front pushing through Friday. Storms could produce locally damaging winds, heavy rain, frequent lightning. 30% chance storms tonight before 1 AM. FOX 7 Austin: 'As much as 2 inches possible in northern Texas; central TX in marginal severe risk.'
Saturday: 50% chance showers/thunderstorms. High near 93°F. Heat index 100-107°F.
Sunday: 20% storms after 1 PM. High near 96°F. South wind 10-15 mph, gusts to 25 mph.
Extended: Hot and humid pattern continues — highs 96–98°F Monday through Wednesday. Mostly sunny after storms clear Saturday.

POOL CLOSURES: Deep Eddy Pool closing Monday. Ramsey, Murchison, and Barton Springs pools CURRENTLY CLOSED. Brief pool guests on alternatives (hotel pool only operational option for many visitors today).

Outdoor event risk: Kali Uchis at Germania Amphitheater (outdoor) and Music Under the Stars at Capitol Mall (outdoor) — monitor NWS EWX for any pre-storm cell development 1–4 PM. Storms expected late tonight, not during peak show hours.

events.name: Kali Uchis — Germania Insurance Amphitheater
events.venue: Germania Insurance Amphitheater, 9201 Circuit of the Americas Blvd
events.detail: Large outdoor amphitheater show with high demand. ~14,000 capacity. Located at COTA, 8.5 mi SE of property — primary traffic impact on I-35 S, Hwy 71, and US-183 beginning 5 PM. Rideshare surge expected 9:30–11 PM post-show. Outdoor venue with storm risk tonight (storms possible after midnight). Monitor NWS EWX for any weather advisory that could affect outdoor event operations.

events.name: Music Under the Stars — Capitol Mall Amphitheater (Juneteenth)
events.venue: Capitol Mall Amphitheater, Bullock Texas State History Museum, 1800 Congress Ave
events.detail: Free Juneteenth concert on the Capitol Mall — Rochelle & the Sidewinders at 7 PM, Tameca Jones at 8 PM. 0.5 mi north of property. Free public event drives large, informal foot traffic on Congress Ave and 11th Street from 6 PM. Expect pedestrian spillover on Cesar Chavez and 2nd Street post-show (9 PM). Property will see elevated walk-in guests seeking dining and bar service after the show.

events.name: A Very Juneteenth Comedy Jam — The Velveeta Room
events.detail: Small comedy venue on 6th Street. Standard 6th Street crowd profile. Low direct impact to property.

events.name: DeRay Davis — Cap City Comedy Club
events.venue: Cap City Comedy Club, 8120 Research Blvd
events.detail: National touring comedian at Cap City. Located north of downtown; no direct impact to property footprint.

events.name: Juneteenth Parade & All-Day Festival — East Austin
events.venue: E. 12th St / MLK Blvd / Rosewood Neighborhood Park
events.detail: Juneteenth Parade 10 AM–noon along E. 12th Street. All-day festival at Rosewood Park. Heavy foot traffic in East Austin all day. Road closures east of I-35 limit eastbound vehicle access. After parade (noon+), crowd disperses toward downtown, Rainey Street, and 6th Street. Expect elevated walk-ins at property early afternoon.

events.name: FIFA World Cup Day 9 — Watch Parties
events.detail: June 19 WC Day 9: USA vs. Australia (3 PM ET, Seattle — FOX); Scotland vs. Morocco (6 PM ET, Foxborough); Brazil vs. Haiti (9 PM ET, Philadelphia); Turkey vs. Paraguay. USA match at 3 PM ET (2 PM CDT) is the most significant watch party draw in Austin. Expect elevated bar/restaurant traffic mid-afternoon. Brazil 9 PM match also draws well at Brazilian-focused venues.

property_actions: JUNETEENTH — ROAD CLOSURES ACTIVE: E. 12th Street / MLK Blvd east of I-35 CLOSED from ~8 AM. Brief valet and concierge: eastbound I-35 access limited. Use alternate routes — Cesar Chavez/MLK from west. All City of Austin, Travis County, and UT offices CLOSED. Anticipate elevated walk-in guest traffic throughout the day.

HEAT ADVISORY IN EFFECT THROUGH SATURDAY EVENING: Heat index up to 106°F today. Maintain hydration stations at valet, pool, and outdoor event areas. Mandatory 30-min outdoor staff breaks continue. Deep Eddy, Ramsey, Murchison, and Barton Springs pools CLOSED — hotel pool is at premium demand. Manage capacity proactively.

ROBBERY-HOMICIDE SUSPECT STILL AT LARGE (E. RIVERSIDE): Brief ALL exterior staff — Hispanic male, 15–20, gray hoodie, light-colored sedan. $1,000 reward active. Report suspicious loitering: APD (512) 974-5000 / Crime Stoppers (512) 472-8477.

MUSIC UNDER THE STARS — CAPITOL MALL AMPHITHEATER (0.5 mi N, 7–9 PM): Free Juneteenth concert, est. 2,000–3,000 attendees. Rochelle & the Sidewinders (7 PM), Tameca Jones (8 PM). Expect significant foot traffic on Congress Ave and 2nd Street/Cesar Chavez from 6 PM. Post-show crowd (9–10 PM) will walk toward Rainey Street and property area. Pre-position exterior staff, ensure entrance is clear.

KALI UCHIS — GERMANIA AMPHITHEATER (~14,000, 7 PM, OUTDOOR): Large outdoor show at COTA. I-35 southbound gridlock expected 5–8 PM (concert start) and 10 PM–midnight (egress). Storm watch: venue is outdoor — if severe cell develops before 10 PM, expect early crowd dispersal toward downtown. Monitor NWS EWX.

US-IRAN MOU PROTEST WATCH — ELEVATED: Burgenstock talks collapsed, Israel resumed Lebanon airstrikes. Elevated risk of spontaneous demonstrations near Capitol or UT campus today. If protest forms and moves toward Congress Ave/Cesar Chavez, notify Director of Security immediately. APD has augmented Juneteenth presence downtown.

FLASH FLOOD WATCH — TONIGHT: Storms possible after midnight (30% chance). Brief overnight valet staff on flood protocol. Ensure drains clear at loading dock and underground parking entrance. Review emergency weather procedures with afternoon/evening shift supervisors.
FIFA WC USA vs. AUSTRALIA (2 PM CDT): Monitor bar district foot traffic 1–4 PM. USA match draws significant crowds to 6th Street sports bars. Elevated guest requests for game viewing recommendations.
national_context: US-IRAN MOU BURGENSTOCK TALKS POSTPONED: Iran's IRGC hardliners objected to a public ceremony with US officials; Iran reportedly suspended 60-day negotiation window. JD Vance cancelled Switzerland trip late Thursday. Swiss Federal Dept of Foreign Affairs confirmed: 'Talks postponed — preparatory work continues.' Cause: Israel resumed Lebanon airstrikes Friday (16+ killed), accusing Hezbollah of ceasefire violations. MOU remains signed (June 18) but fragile. Strait of Hormuz still open per existing MOU terms. Elevated domestic protest watch — both pro-Palestinian and pro-deal factions may react.

JUNETEENTH — FEDERAL & STATE HOLIDAY: June 19 marks 161 years since Maj. Gen. Gordon Granger announced freedom for enslaved people in Texas (1865). Federal holiday observed nationwide. Austin's Juneteenth Parade on E. 12th Street; festival at Rosewood Park; free concert at Capitol Mall Amphitheater 7–9 PM. City of Austin, Travis County, UT Austin all closed.

FIFA WC DAY 9: USA vs. Australia (3 PM ET, Lumen Field Seattle — FOX). Scotland vs. Morocco (6 PM ET). Brazil vs. Haiti (9 PM ET). USA match is highest watch party draw in Austin. No Austin Q2 Stadium matches today.

TROPICAL STORM ARTHUR AFTERMATH: Remnants pushed inland through SE Texas / western Louisiana. Flash flood risk from Arthur's moisture plume: Level 2/4 for central TX Friday. 5–10 inches of rain possible from upper TX coast through Louisiana/Mississippi. Austin impact: elevated storm risk late Friday, residual moisture through weekend.

ISRAEL-LEBANON: Israel resumed airstrikes on Lebanon Friday (16+ killed), accusing Hezbollah of violating ceasefire terms. Iran threatened to collapse the MOU unless Israel halts attacks. Situation fluid — monitor for rapid escalation or de-escalation over weekend.
lookaheads: 50% chance showers/thunderstorms Saturday. High 93°F, heat index 100–107°F. After today's residual moisture, brief intense cells possible. Monitor NWS EWX for flash flood watch. Review valet and outdoor event protocols for wet conditions.

Germania Amphitheater likely has additional weekend events; Moody Center and ACL Live calendar should be checked for Saturday shows. High foot traffic on 6th Street and Rainey Street as Juneteenth weekend continues. Expect elevated hotel occupancy.
SUN Jun 21 — Father's Day + Summer Solstice
Father's Day — expect elevated F&B covers for Sunday brunch and dinner. High near 96°F, gusts to 25 mph. Summer Solstice. 20% storm chance after 1 PM.
MON–WED Jun 22–24 — Sustained Heat Wave Returns

Highs 97–98°F Monday through Wednesday, mostly sunny. Heat protocols should remain active all week. Deep Eddy Pool closes Monday — hotel pool will see significantly elevated demand from guests seeking relief.

Iran IRGC hardliners actively threatening to collapse the MOU. Israel attacks in Lebanon are the stated trigger. 60-day negotiation window at risk. Elevated protest watch ongoing through the weekend near Capitol and UT campus. Cyber threat posture: maintain elevated vigilance during geopolitical instability.
